object_types.name: SpendTier

object_types.name: RiskReview
object_types.definition: A signed-off review record assessing a vendor's risk, created on a re-review cycle; each review belongs to exactly one vendor.

source_references.excerpt: The review is its own record. It has a review ID, because we need to know who signed it and when, and auditors ask. It's not a checkbox on the vendor.

ambiguities.description: Both Dana's 'spend tier' and Raj's 'risk tier' are colloquially called 'tier', causing confusion in meetings. The model treats them as two distinct fields (SpendTier and RiskTier), but the transcript notes this naming battle has never been fully resolved organizationally -- worth confirming the final field names used in the system to avoid ongoing confusion.

source_references.excerpt: And you both call it "tier." ... We've asked people to say spend tier and risk tier. Nobody does. It's been a losing battle for two years.

ambiguities.description: The rule that procurement has actually been following (W-9/tax form as the gate to active status, allowing PO creation) contradicts the officially enforced system rule (risk review required for active status). It's unclear whether this is purely a training/communication gap or whether there is some other undocumented workflow path that needs to be modeled.

source_references.excerpt: Tax form on file. Once the W-9 is in, they're live and a buyer can raise a PO. ... I know they have. I've watched it happen. But the system does enforce it -- you cannot move a vendor to active without a completed review, the transition is blocked.

ambiguities.description: What happens to in-flight purchase orders when a vendor is suspended (e.g., a proposed 'run-off' status) is explicitly parked as an unresolved policy decision pending the sourcing steering group and Legal. No constraint or additional status was agreed, so the model does not capture post-suspension PO fulfillment behavior.

source_references.excerpt: Then we need a middle state. Something like run-off -- existing POs complete, no new ones can be raised. ... I'm not agreeing to a fourth status in this room, off the cuff, without Legal.

ambiguities.description: Vendor has three addresses (remit-to, ship-from, legal) which are 'frequently different and frequently wrong.' These were mentioned but not modeled in detail as separate fact types/value types since the transcript did not elaborate further on their structure or constraints -- should each address be a structured entity (street/city/etc.) and are all three mandatory or optional?

source_references.excerpt: Address, though we have three addresses really -- remit-to, ship-from, and the legal one, which are frequently different and frequently wrong.

ambiguities.description: Mei maintains an unofficial spreadsheet tracking a 'preferred vendor' flag and other notes (stale contacts, informal payment terms). This was explicitly excluded from the model per Mei's request ('It's ad hoc. Don't model it.') but represents a known gap between actual practice and the system of record.

source_references.excerpt: There's a column called "preferred." It means if two vendors can supply the same thing, buy from this one. It's not in the system anywhere. It's just my column. ... It's ad hoc. Don't model it.
